title: active-gel fed comets do not divide: across zeta 40-60, ks 0.02-0.05 and Da 3-4 the population is replenished only by nucleation (0 persistent splits in 11 runs), and below the uniform-state threshold the comets cannot persist
summary: I looked for division in the fed-comet world (contractile active-gel flow, generator made from a regrowing substrate, self-laid regulator trail). In 11 labkit runs (zeta 40-60, substrate regrowth ks 0.02-0.05, Da 3-4, 2-3 seeds each, T=200-300) the comets keep ~5 px bodies and swim (22-56 moving tracks per run), but there are 0 persistent splits; the 1-35 raw splits re-merge, and new comets come from nucleation (51-150 per run) in substrate-rich gaps, while collisions fuse comets (merges 37-149). When the uniform fed state is made linearly stable (ks=0.02 with zeta 40-50) no comet survives at all, so in this family comets exist only where the background also nucleates new ones: spontaneous generation, not reproduction. Division will need a growth-limited body that is larger than one contractile focus (e.g. a conserved generator pool per body, or a regulator that accumulates at the head centre faster than the comet escapes it).

finding.operator: contractile active-gel advection of an autocatalytic, substrate-fed stress generator with a self-laid regulator trail
finding.control: parameter scan over zeta, ks, Da with labkit lineage (merge-aware persistent splits) on 2-3 seeds each
finding.result: 0 persistent splits in 11 runs; nucleations 51-150 and merges 37-149 per run; ks=0.02 with zeta<=50: all comets die by t~90
